subject: Risk & Compliance
title: HSBC and the Cartels
description: A 60-second lesson on HSBC and the Cartels.

hook.text: HSBC processed $881 million for drug cartels. Tellers in Mexico used specially sized boxes to fit the deposit window.

buildup.text: Mexican cartels deposited cash directly into HSBC accounts. The bank's compliance team was overwhelmed and ignored.

discovery.text: A US Senate investigation revealed HSBC had failed to monitor $60 trillion in wire transfers.

twist.text: HSBC paid $1.9 billion in fines but no executives went to prison. The bank was 'too big to jail.'

climax.text: When the penalty for laundering billions is a fine, the fine becomes a cost of doing business.

punchline.text: $881 million laundered. $1.9 billion fine. Zero jail time.

quiz.question: What happened to HSBC executives after the cartel laundering scandal?
options: The CEO was extradited to Mexico
